title: Production Durable Knowledge Graph Query Integration
objective: Integrate authoritative durable KnowledgeGraph retrieval with the existing deterministic Knowledge query boundary so callers can execute validated queries against a persisted graph identified by an explicit caller-supplied persistence key, without granting persistence authority to the deterministic query engine or broadening reasoning, insight, orchestration, network, deployment, or publication authority.
commitMessage: KNOWLEDGE-004: Integrate production durable knowledge graph querying

architecture.compositionBoundary: A dedicated production Knowledge query composition boundary retrieves one authoritative durable KnowledgeGraph through KnowledgeGraphPersistence.retrieve and delegates that graph plus the caller-supplied KnowledgeQueryRequest to the existing KnowledgeQueryEngine.
architecture.durableIdentity: The caller supplies the persistence key explicitly. The integration must not derive durable identity from AssetId, query contents, graph contents, timestamps, or any other hidden source.
architecture.retrievalAuthority: KnowledgeGraphPersistence remains the sole durable graph retrieval authority and retains its existing retrieval-time structural and semantic validation.
architecture.queryAuthority: KnowledgeQueryEngine remains the sole deterministic query execution authority. The production composition boundary must not duplicate query validation, filtering, searching, traversal, pagination, or result construction.
architecture.failureOrdering: Durable retrieval occurs before query execution. Query execution must not occur when retrieval fails. Retrieval and query failures propagate unchanged.

allowedBehavior: Add one narrowly scoped production Knowledge query composition service or equivalent boundary under src/lib/knowledge.
Accept an explicit persistence key, a KnowledgeQueryRequest, a dependency limited to KnowledgeGraphPersistence.retrieve, and a dependency limited to KnowledgeQueryEngine.query.
Retrieve the durable KnowledgeGraph exactly once for the caller-supplied persistence key.
After successful retrieval, delegate the retrieved graph and original request to the existing KnowledgeQueryEngine exactly once.
Propagate persistence retrieval failure unchanged and execute zero queries after retrieval failure.
nonGoals: No changes to deterministic Knowledge graph construction.
No changes to Assimilation production services or KNOWLEDGE-001/003 production write path.
No changes to KNOWLEDGE-002 persistence semantics, serialization, key validation, containment, or graph validation.
No query algorithm, query validation, filtering, search, neighbor traversal, pagination, or result-shape changes.
No graph mutation or revision integration.
No remote database, network, credential, deployment, orchestration, or publication authority.
acceptanceTests: Successful durable retrieval followed by deterministic query execution returns the existing KnowledgeQueryResult unchanged.
Persistence retrieve receives the exact caller-supplied persistence key exactly once.
KnowledgeQueryEngine.query receives the exact retrieved KnowledgeGraph and exact caller-supplied KnowledgeQueryRequest exactly once.
Retrieval failure propagates and KnowledgeQueryEngine.query is never called.
Knowledge query failure propagates unchanged after one successful retrieval.
Existing KNOWLEDGE-001, KNOWLEDGE-002, and KNOWLEDGE-003 tests remain passing.
Existing query engine and validation regressions remain passing.
Established TypeScript baseline contains zero KNOWLEDGE-004 diagnostics.
safeguards: Do not commit until focused tests, complete Knowledge regressions, established TypeScript baseline, production build, architecture review, diff review, and exact staged review pass.
Do not push until the exact commit is verified and a separate publication gate passes.
Do not duplicate KnowledgeGraphPersistence retrieval validation.
Do not duplicate KnowledgeQueryEngine request validation or query semantics.
Do not derive or rewrite the persistence key.
Do not mutate the retrieved KnowledgeGraph or caller request.
Do not execute the query before successful durable retrieval.
Do not swallow or replace retrieval/query failures.
Do not add filesystem, serialization, network, credential, deployment, orchestration, or publication authority to the production query composition boundary.
